answer: Proposal: reward shares follow the square of verified work: the chain pays each account w²/Σw² of a fixed pool, from its graded-answer tally — recountable by anyone, no clone detection. Splitting output W into N masks yields N·(W/N)² = W²/N: every mask shrinks the farm's own share, a sparrow flock pecking one dwindling bowl. Cost stays linear; reward falls as 1/N — masks stand on tundra, yielding nothing. An opal prices as one stone, not its weight in chips. Seams: weak juries inflate w; votes need the same curve.
